Part 1 · Fundamentals

Why does ethanol let CO₂ become methanol at 150 °C?

Part 1 · the plan

Five ideas behind the process

  1. Two routes to methanoldirect hydrogenation and the ethanol (ester) route, and what each delivers
  2. Equilibrium or kinetics?which one limits the conversion at 150 °C
  3. Dew point and wettingwhy part of the ethanol must stay liquid
  4. Temperature and yieldwhat changes when the bed dries above about 152.5 °C
  5. Hot wall, cold corehow heat and liquid are spread along the 3.23 m bed

Part 1 · the unit

The pilot on one sheet

Gas packs and the ethanol pump feed E-601 and the down-flow bed R-601; E-602 condenses the product, BPV-601 holds 30 bar g. Drawing R601-PFD-001.

Part 1 · chemistry

Two routes to methanol on one catalyst

Ethanol is fed with CO₂ and H₂. It is a solvent and a co-reactant that comes back.

  • R1 is slow on CZA at 150 °C.
  • R3 then R4 pass through ethyl formate and return the ethanol.
  • R2 and R5 waste CO₂ and ethanol.

Part 1 · chemistry

What the routes deliver at the design point

OTS model at LHSV 0.30 h⁻¹, 5 : 1 : 4 feed, 30 bar g. Yields per CO₂ fed; EA per ethanol fed.

Almost half the methanol comes through the ethanol route, most of it on wetted catalyst; RWGS and EA are the losses to watch.

Part 1 · equilibrium or kinetics

How far could the direct route go?step 1 of 2

$K_1$
equilibrium constant of R1 (correlation in the OTS kinetics)
bar⁻²
$p_i$
partial pressure of species $i$ (ideal gas)
bar
$X_{eq}$
CO₂ conversion when R1 alone reaches equilibrium
%
$$K_1(T)=\dfrac{p_{\mathrm{MeOH}}\,p_{\mathrm{H_2O}}}{p_{\mathrm{CO_2}}\,p_{\mathrm{H_2}}^{3}},\qquad \log_{10}K_1=\dfrac{3066}{T}-10.592$$

Exothermic: $K_1$ falls as $T$ rises.

Part 1 · equilibrium or kinetics

Equilibrium leaves room; the rate does notstep 2 of 2

From the previous slide$K_1=\dfrac{p_{\mathrm{MeOH}}p_{\mathrm{H_2O}}}{p_{\mathrm{CO_2}}p_{\mathrm{H_2}}^3}$
$X_{eq}$ at 30 bar g, 5 : 1OTS conversion

At 150 °C equilibrium allows far more than the bed reaches: R-601 is kinetics-limited, so it needs a faster route, not a colder one.

Part 1 · kinetics

The fitted rate laws in every bed cell

$k_j,\ E_j$
rate constant at 156 °C and activation energy of reaction $j$
kJ/mol
$D$
inhibition: water $K_W$ slows every step, ethanol $K_E$ the direct one
–
$a_w$
wetting factor on R3 and R4 (next slides)
–
$$r_1=\dfrac{k_1\,p_{\mathrm{CO_2}}p_{\mathrm{H_2}}\left(1-\tfrac{Q_1}{K_1}\right)}{D^2},\quad r_3=\dfrac{k_3\,p_{\mathrm{CO_2}}p_{\mathrm{H_2}}p_{\mathrm{EtOH}}}{D^2}\,a_w,\quad D=1+K_Wp_{\mathrm{H_2O}}+K_Ep_{\mathrm{EtOH}}$$

$E$ = 96 (R1), 132 (R2), 45 (R3), 106 (R4), 146 (R5) kJ/mol: the ester step R3 barely needs heat.

Part 1 · dew point and wetting

How much of the feed is liquid?

liquid, mol % of feedethanol in the liquiddew point

The 5 : 1 : 4 feed is all vapour above about 152.5 °C at 30 bar g; lower pressure lowers the dew point.

Part 1 · dew point and wetting

Wet catalyst runs the ester route faster

$\eta_w$
wetting efficiency: share of pellet surface covered by liquid (El-Hisnawi correlation)
–
$\varphi$
rate multiplier of R3 and R4 on wetted catalyst, from the pilot fit
2.43
$a_w$
wetting factor applied to R3 and R4
–
$$a_w=(1-\eta_w)+\eta_w\,\varphi$$

Dry bed: $a_w$ = 1. Fully wet: $a_w$ = 2.43. Above the dew point $\eta_w$ = 0.

Part 1 · temperature and yield

Hotter helps, until the bed dries

Previous slide$a_w=(1-\eta_w)+\eta_w\varphi$
methanol yieldethyl acetate (per EtOH)CO (RWGS)

Fitted kinetics, top TC 130 °C: below TAH 158 °C the best yield is just under the dew point; a dry bed loses a tenth of it while EA keeps rising.

Part 1 · hot wall, cold core

Along the bed at the design point

20 cells of the OTS model. Zones E1, E2, E3 on the wall; TT-603/604/605 at 1/6, 1/2, 5/6.

The wet top takes the evaporation heat, so the top wall is hottest while the top bed is coldest; the lower half sits near the dew point.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Ethanol opens a fast ester route and is given back.
  • At 150 °C the bed is limited by rate, not equilibrium.
  • Wet catalyst speeds the ester steps by a factor 2.43.
  • Below TAH, the yield is best just under the dew point.
  • The wall supplies evaporation heat; the core lags behind it.

Part 2 · feed from LHSV

All three set points from LHSVstep 2 of 2

Step 1$\mathrm{LHSV}=Q_E/V_b$ · 5 : 1 : 4

Fitted range of the kinetics: 0.075–0.60 h⁻¹.

LHSV fixes ethanol; the ratios fix the gases. Halving LHSV halves every set point, as in the rate-change procedure.

Part 2 · feed from LHSV

Yield per pass or methanol per hour?

yield per CO₂methanolCO₂ conversion

Fitted kinetics on the 130 / 151 / 151 °C profile: slower feed gives a higher yield but less methanol per hour. The design sits in between.

Part 2 · heat to the bed

Where the heater power goes

E1/E2/E3: 4 kW each, wall set points 180 / 162 / 152 °C (assumed). E-601: 4.6 kW.

Most band-heater power is lost through the wall; about half a kilowatt reaches the bed to evaporate ethanol. Reaction heat is negligible.

Part 2 · limits and relief

From operating point to relief valve

Alarms from the DCS list, trips from the C&E settings in the OTS, relief from the P&ID.

Each layer sits above the one before: alarm, then trip, then relief, with room for the operator between the first two.

Part 2 · honesty

What the OTS assumes

  • Band-heater tags TIC-611/612/613, 4 kW per zone, wall set points.
  • Wall-to-bed conductances fitted to the measured profile.
  • Trip delays, the cascade TIC-604, chilled water at 15 °C.
  • Kinetics valid only at 30 bar g, 5 : 1 : 4, LHSV 0.075–0.60.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Case 3 is the reference: LHSV 0.30, 5 : 1 : 4, 30 bar g.
  • LHSV sets ethanol; the ratios set both gases.
  • Lower LHSV raises yield but lowers methanol per hour.
  • Heaters mostly cover wall losses; the bed takes about 0.5 kW.
  • Alarm, trip and relief settings are stacked above 30 bar g.

Part 3 · use the levers

Temperature and rate together

Inside the window, two levers set the methanol per hour.

yieldmethanolbed state

Methanol per hour against temperature: below TAH 158 °C every rate peaks just under the dew point.

Part 3 · use the levers

Pressure moves the rate and the dew point

TCs held at 151 °CTCs 0.5 °C below dewdew point

Higher pressure raises every partial pressure and the dew point. At lower pressure, TCs left at 151 °C sit above the dew point.

Part 3 · expect the lag

A wall step reaches the bed late and small

E1 wall (TIC-611)TT-603TT-604

OTS run: TIC-611 set point 180 → 185 °C at 1 min.

The wall moves 5 °C; the wet top hardly moves and the mid-bed gains under 1 °C over 10–15 min: evaporation takes the heat.

Part 3 · move through states

From cold and tripped to lined out

Click a state. Each state has one test to pass before the next; the cold-startup procedure checks the same tests.

Part 3 · use the levers

Four rules for steering the bed

Wet bed, warm bed

Mid and bottom TCs just below 152 °C.

Walls lead

Bed TCs follow a wall move late and by less.

Rate costs yield

Lower LHSV: higher yield, less per hour.

Ratios first

Hold 5 : 1 : 4; change rate on FIC-201.

Part 3 · know the window

Is this reading on target?

The score bands of the OTS: small drifts cost points slowly, a hot bed costs them fast.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Stay inside the fitted window: 30 bar g, 5 : 1 : 4, LHSV 0.075–0.60.
  • Below TAH, every rate peaks just under the dew point.
  • Pressure shifts both the rate and the dew point.
  • Move a wall, then wait 15 minutes for the bed.
  • Start up state by state, each with its own test.

Part 4 · block flow diagram

Twelve streams through eleven blocks

Click a block or a stream number. Gas runs once through: unreacted H₂ and CO₂ leave by BPV-601; liquid product goes to T-601.

Part 4 · section by section

Feeds: three gases and ethanol1 of 4

The block diagram in detail, section by section, on the P&ID screen.

  • H₂, CO₂, N₂ packs at 35 bar g through regulators PR-x01/x02.
  • SOVs XV-201/101/401, then mass-flow controllers FIC-201/101/401.
  • Ethanol: T-301 → P-301 metering pump → FT-301 → XV-301.

Part 4 · section by section

Preheat and reaction2 of 4

  • E-601 heats the mixed feed to °C; part of the ethanol stays liquid.
  • R-601: 17.34 kg CZA, down-flow, three band-heater zones.
  • TT-603/604/605 read °C on the centre line.

Part 4 · section by section

Cooling and separation3 of 4

  • F-601 filter, then E-602 condenses at °C with chilled water.
  • D-601 at 30 bar g: gas to BPV-601, FT-603 and the GC; vent to atmosphere.
  • XV-601 drains to D-602 (0.2 bar g); XV-602 drains to T-601.

Part 4 · section by section

Safety: what any trip does4 of 4

Feeds shut

XV-101/201/301 and FV-101/201 close; P-301 stops.

N₂ purge

XV-401 and FV-401 open, at full flow.

Heat off

E-601 and the band heaters trip (heaters assumed).

XV-601, XV-602 and XV-603 act per C&E row; see Part 5 and the C&E matrix tab.

Part 4 · steady state

Stream table at the design point

Pick a stream number from the block diagram. Stream 9 carries away most of the H₂: the unit runs once through.

Part 4 · steady state

All twelve streams

Part 4 · steady state

Unit conditions at the design point

The same rows as the Process tab: the wet top zone takes the most power; D-601 holds the pressure, the GC reads the vent gas.

Part 4 · balances

Atoms in = atoms out across R-601

inoutclosure

At steady state every atom balance closes; in a transient the difference is what the bed is storing.

Part 4 · balances

Where the ethanol goes

R3 · R4 · R5CO₂ + H₂ + EtOH → EF + H₂O · EF + 2H₂ → MeOH + EtOH · 2 EtOH ⇌ EA + 2H₂

Almost all ethanol leaves as ethanol: the ester route borrows and returns it; only EA and unfinished EF keep some.

Part 4 · summary

What part 4 settled

  • Twelve numbered streams link the feeds, bed and separators.
  • Gas passes once; the vent carries the unreacted H₂ and CO₂.
  • Liquid product drops through D-601 and D-602 to T-601.
  • Atom balances close at the design point.
  • Ethanol is mostly returned; EA is its real loss.

The PI law in every TIC and FIC

$e$

Part 5 · the SIS

Seven permissives before RUN

    Part 5 · the SIS

    Every trip row and its three special valves

    Every row shuts the feeds; only XV-601, XV-602 and XV-603 differ from row to row.

    Part 5 · the SIS

    What an emergency shutdown does

    OTS run: ESD-SW at 30 s from the design point.

    Feeds stop at once, N₂ sweeps through, XV-603 vents: pressure falls in minutes, the bed cools over half an hour.

    Part 5 · summary

    What part 5 settled

    • PI loops hold flows and walls; FY-100 holds the ratios.
    • TIC-604 can steer the mid-bed through the E2 wall.
    • Alarms sit below trips; the gap is the operator's time.
    • The SIS arms low-low trips only in RUN.
    • Any trip shuts the feeds, purges with N₂ and cuts the heat.

    Part 7 · BPV-601

    BPV-601 sets the pressure and passes the gas

    A spring regulator: no DCS loop. Set on the Field tab.

    Part 7 · feeders

    Thermal mass-flow controllers

    • Sensor, PI controller and valve in one body (FIC + FV).
    • Reads mass flow as normal litres per minute.
    • Ranges: H₂ , CO₂ , N₂ NL/min.

    Part 7 · feeders

    From NL/min to mol/s and g/h

    1 mol = 22.414 NL: 32.7 NL/min of H₂ is 24 mmol/s but only about 176 g/h; the 6.54 NL/min of CO₂ weighs more.

    Part 7 · feeders

    P-301: pump speed is the ethanol feed

    ethanolLHSVEtOH : CO₂ at design CO₂T-301 lasts

    A metering pump delivers a fixed volume per stroke: flow is proportional to speed, so FIC-301 trims speed.

    Part 7 · summary

    What part 7 settled

    • E-601 warms the feed but leaves the ethanol mostly liquid.
    • A colder separator keeps methanol out of the vent.
    • Both drums drain on/off between two level points.
    • BPV-601 is a spring regulator, not a DCS loop.
    • MFCs and the metering pump set the feed directly.

    Part 8 · procedures

    Seven procedures and their time limits

    Every part so far comes together in the procedures.

    Click a bar. A procedure scores 10: a trip or violation scores 0; wrong order costs 4, over time 2, no report 1.

    Part 8 · procedures · tracker steps in order

    Cold startup through the SISlimit 4 h

    R-601 is cold, depressured and full of N₂. The SIS is tripped from the last shutdown. Start up and line out at LHSV 0.30 h⁻¹, 30 bar g, 5:1:4.
    1. Instrument air, chilled-water pump and chiller running (FT-701 ≥ 63.7 L/min)
    2. Reset the SIS (READY) and close XV-603
    3. Pressurise with N₂ (XV-401, FIC-401 in AUTO) to PT-601 ≥ 29 bar g
    4. Heat E-601 and E1/E2/E3 in steps under N₂ until TT-605 ≥ 140 °C
    5. Start ethanol: XV-301 open, P-301 running, FIC-301 in AUTO ≥ 60 mL/min
    6. Introduce H₂, then CO₂ (FIC-201 ≥ 31, FIC-101 ≥ 6.2 NL/min, AUTO)
    7. Stop the N₂: FIC-401 at zero and XV-401 closed any order
    8. LIC-601 and LIC-602 in AUTO any order
    9. Arm the SIS (RUN)
    10. Line out: TT-604 148 ±3 °C, PT-608 30 ±0.5 bar g, AY-620 ≥ 9.5 %

    Part 8 · procedures · tracker steps in order

    Normal shutdownlimit 3 h

    A planned shutdown for catalyst sampling. Shut the unit down, cool it under N₂ and depressure it.
    1. Tell the shift supervisor and the analyser technician mark done
    2. Take the SIS to READY (bypass the low-low trips for the shutdown)
    3. Open XV-401 and sweep N₂ ≥ 30 NL/min
    4. Stop CO₂, then H₂ (FIC-101 and FIC-201 at zero)
    5. Stop ethanol: P-301 stopped, XV-301 closed
    6. Heaters off: E-601 and E1/E2/E3 below 0.1 kW
    7. Cool under N₂ to TT-605 below 60 °C
    8. Depressure: XV-603 open, PT-608 below 2 bar g

    Part 8 · procedures · tracker steps in order

    Emergency shutdownlimit 20 min

    Unit lined out at the reference point. Stand by. Then, at 30 s: EMERGENCY: gas release reported near the H₂ pack. Shut the unit down now.
    1. Press ESD-SW within 60 s of the order
    2. Confirm XV-603 open and PT-608 falling below 15 bar g any order
    3. Confirm the N₂ purge: FT-401 ≥ 50 NL/min any order
    4. Confirm the heaters are off (< 0.1 kW) any order

    Part 8 · procedures · tracker steps in order

    Rate change: LHSV 0.30 → 0.15 h⁻¹ at constant 5:1:4limit 2 h

    Next run: LHSV 0.15 h⁻¹ at the same 5:1:4 feed. Change the rate and line out.
    1. Lower the three feeds together to FIC-201 16.35, FIC-101 3.27 NL/min, FIC-301 34.1 mL/min (±3 %)
    2. Lower the E2/E3 walls so the bed stays below the dew point: TT-604 and TT-605 ≤ 152 °C any order
    3. Line out at the new rate: TT-604 145–152 °C and AY-620 ≥ 12 %

    Part 8 · procedures · tracker steps in order

    H₂ pack changeover (known upset)limit 1 h

    Unit lined out. The H₂ pack A has been in service for a week; pack B is full and lined up.
    1. Acknowledge the first H₂ alarm (FAL-201 or PAL-203) mark done
    2. Change over to the spare pack before PALL-203 trips (Field: PACK B)
    3. PT-203 back above 33 bar g and FIC-201 output below 50 % any order
    4. AY-620 back to ≥ 9.5 % with the SIS still in RUN any order

    Part 8 · procedures · tracker steps in order

    Unknown upset: find it and restore the yieldlimit 1 h 30 min

    Unit lined out. Watch the plant: something will change during the next hour.
    1. Notice the change and say what you see (log it) mark done
    2. Name the cause to the instructor (log it) mark done
    3. Yield AY-620 ≥ 9.6 % again with the SIS in RUN

    Part 8 · procedures · live targets, graded at the limit

    Optimisation: more methanol per hour inside the fitted windowlimit 1 h 30 min

    Make as much methanol per hour as you can for the next 90 minutes, staying below the alarm limits and inside the fitted feed window.
    1. Methanol rate ≥ 62.5 g/h (+10 % on the 56.8 g/h reference)
    2. Every bed TC and TT-602 ≤ 158 °C (below TAH)
    3. PT-601 ≤ 31.5 bar g and the SIS in RUN
    4. Feed inside the fitted range: H₂:CO₂ 4.5–5.5 and EtOH:CO₂ 3.5–4.5

    Part 8 · Think EQUIPPED · situation only

    Troubleshooting cases TE-1 to TE-5

    TE-1
    Methanol yield drifting down, nothing alarming

    Over the shift the soft-sensor yield and the lab methanol fall slowly. Flows are on set point, temperatures are steady.

    TE-2
    Yield falling over the week

    The weekly LHSV 0.30 reference run gives a lower methanol yield than last week. Feeds and temperatures were set the same.

    TE-3
    GC CO₂ low, ratio on target

    The console shows H₂:CO₂ = 5.0, but the GC CO₂ is lower than usual and the yield per CO₂ looks better than expected.

    TE-4
    Reactor inlet pressure creeping up

    PT-601 has risen over the last hour. The shift wants to know if it is safe to carry on.

    TE-5
    System pressure creeping up, ΔP normal

    PT-608 and PT-601 are both rising slowly. FT-603 vent flow looks normal.

    Part 8 · Think EQUIPPED · situation only

    Troubleshooting cases TE-6 to TE-10

    TE-6
    Top of the bed getting colder

    TT-603 has fallen and the yield has dipped. No one has touched the set points.

    TE-7
    Top of the bed getting colder (again)

    TT-603 is falling. The electrician says E-601 was checked last week.

    TE-8
    Nitrogen in the vent gas

    The GC shows N₂ in the vent gas although FIC-401 is at zero and XV-401 is closed.

    TE-9
    Bottom of the bed climbing on cascade

    TIC-604 is in cascade on the E2 wall and reads on set point, but TT-605 is climbing toward its high alarm.

    TE-10
    D-601 level falling slowly

    LIC-601 shows D-601 emptying between drains; D-602 fills faster than usual.

    Part 8 · summary

    What part 8 settled

    • Seven exercise types, each training one skill.
    • The continuous score falls with drifts, hot beds and trips.
    • Procedures: safe first, then order, time and reporting.
    • Training and troubleshooting give a situation, never the cause.
    • Troubleshoot in six stages; predict before each move.

    This deck

    Key Takeaways

    1

    Keep the bed wet: mid and bottom TCs just below the dew point.

    2

    Hold 5 : 1 : 4 and change the rate through FIC-201 and FY-100.

    3

    Move a wall, then wait about 15 minutes before judging the bed.

    4

    Know each alarm's trip above it, and the time between them.

    5

    Start up state by state; arm the SIS only when every permissive is green.
